Mission:

We are looking for an enthusiastic and technically capable Additive Manufacturing Technician to join our growing Manufacturing team.

This is a hands-on role where you will help establish and operate TEKEVER's additive manufacturing capability, supporting everything from rapid prototypes and engineering development through to production components for our Aerospace and Defence systems.

You will take ownership of additive manufacturing jobs from build preparation through to finished component, working closely with Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering and Quality.

If you enjoy solving manufacturing problems, working with advanced technology and seeing an idea turn into a physical component, this is an opportunity to make a real impact.

Role & Responsibilities

- Operate and maintain industrial additive manufacturing equipment, including SLS and polymer-based systems.

- Prepare, set up and execute additive manufacturing builds.

- Prepare build files, optimise component orientation and maximise build utilisation.

- Manage material and powder preparation, handling and traceability.

- Depowder, clean and post-process manufactured components.

- Inspect components and identify manufacturing defects or dimensional issues.

- Maintain accurate production, machine and material records.

- Support prototype, R&D and production programmes.

- Work with engineers to develop new additive manufacturing processes and applications.

- Support Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM) activities.7

- Help develop build parameters and manufacturing processes for new components.

- Investigate build failures and implement improvements.

- Support the introduction of new additive manufacturing technologies and equipment.

- Maintain equipment, carry out routine operator maintenance and ensure machines remain production-ready.

- Ensure all work complies with company quality, safety and manufacturing procedures.

- Support FAIRs, inspection documentation, NCRs and full component traceability.

- Identify opportunities to improve machine utilisation, build quality, repeatability and material efficiency.

Essential Skills

- Previous experience working with industrial additive manufacturing / 3D printing equipment.

- Practical manufacturing experience.

- Ability to understand engineering drawings and manufacturing instructions.

- Good understanding of dimensional tolerances and component quality.

- Strong attention to detail.

- A methodical approach to production and documentation.

- Good problem-solving skills.

- Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary engineering team.

Desirable

- SLS additive manufacturing, particularly PA12.

- EOS, 3D Systems or similar industrial AM equipment.

- Additive manufacturing build preparation and nesting software.

- Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM).

- Aerospace or defence manufacturing.

- AS9100 / AS9102.

- FAIR production.

- GD&T.

- CMM or 3D scanning inspection.

- CNC machining.

- MRP/ERP systems and digital manufacturing traceability.

- Metallic additive manufacturing.

At TEKEVER, we offer a comprehensive package designed to reward, support, and develop our people. This includes a highly competitive salary with a discretionary annual bonus and a company pension contribution match of up to 10%. To support your wellbeing, we provide 25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, Private Medical Insurance (with optional family cover), Private Dental care, and an Employee Assistance Programme. We are deeply committed to investing in future talent; our scale allows us to provide clear career development opportunities and dedicated initiatives to boost your skill sets, ensuring you remain future-ready for the evolving workplace. title: AI Documentation Engineer | AR5
AI Technical Writer
description:
Where? Hybrid between Lisboa & Caldas da Rainha

The role

You will own how technical knowledge is captured and turned into certified documentation across the AR5 product team. This is not passive writing or pure prompt engineering: you enable our product engineers to generate documentation directly from their own work using TEKEVER's internal LLM tools, while acting as the accountable human-in-the-loop who guarantees accuracy and compliance. In short, you are a force multiplier for the engineering team, making technical writing a by-product of engineering work rather than a downstream burden.

What you will do

- Enable engineers to produce AR5 documentation with our internal LLM tools, providing the structure, templates, and review that turn raw knowledge into release-quality output;

- Act as the human-in-the-loop: validate and correct AI-generated content for technical accuracy and compliance with aerospace, defence, and UAS certification standards;

- Build and maintain documentation templates, authoring standards, and knowledge-capture practices (structured notes, design rationale) that feed our tooling;

- Govern the full AR5 documentation baseline: structure, version control, traceability, single source of truth;

- Collaborate across systems engineering, avionics/firmware, RF, payload (EO/IR, radar, AIS, SIGINT), and quality teams.

What you bring

- Degree in Aerospace, Electronic, Electrotechnical, or Systems Engineering, or similar;

- Proven experience in a technical role in aerospace, defence, or UAS/autonomous systems, such as documentation engineer, technical writer, or systems engineer;

- Knowledge of avionics, embedded systems, RF, and payload integration, and the ability to read schematics and protocols (MIL-STD, MAVLink, STANAG, or similar);

- Comfort with AI/LLM tooling, version control, and docs-as-code, or strong aptitude to adopt them;

- Excellent technical English, paired with the judgment to validate AI output.

What we have to offer you

• A dynamic and collaborative working environment, with the opportunity to make a real impact
• A competitive salary package, aligned with your proven level of experience
• Meal allowance and health insurance for employees
• Shuttle transport service to the offices in Leiria, Caldas da Rainha and Ponte de Sor

Mission:

Build and run the composites manufacturing capability for Tekever UK Swindon Site drone structure manufacture. From concept to a fully equipped and staffed cell producing the composite airframes and structures that go into every aircraft we build.

This is a build-it-from-scratch role. You will outline the space, how the product is made, recruit the team and then drive to hit the production rate the business needs. You will own the area end to end: layout and footprint, pre-preg lay-up capability, material, tooling, mould control and trimming and finishing.

You will spend your time on the shop floor as much as at a desk. Priorities such as outlined lay-up and cure layouts, interviewing and onboarding your team, creating dedicated trim and inspection cells and driving production to hit rate. You will also work across our European plant network, drawing on proven layouts, processes and lessons learned from sites that are already established and building the supply chain relationships needed to outsource key materials and components where it makes sense to do so.

Key Responsibilities

Facility design and footprint

- Outline the space allocation and factory footprint for composites manufacture — layout, workflow, material flow, climate-controlled lay-up and clean areas, cure, trim, inspection and storage.

- Source and commission the equipment, tooling and fixtures needed to build composite structures at target rate such as cutting tables, autoclaves/ovens, vacuum bagging equipment, trim booths and inspection equipment. Partner with Facilities, Manufacturing Engineering and Supply Chain on selection and installation.

- Plan the physical build-out in phases, aligned to the wider factory ramp and production milestones.

- Visit and benchmark our established production plants across Europe, and translate proven layouts, equipment choices and ways of working into the design of the facility.

- Deploy the dedicated cure, trim and inspection cells specifying equipment, safety systems, instrumentation, data capture and processes.

Composite lay-up and material process ownership

- Own laminate schedules, resin systems, fibre (carbon, glass, aramid) and core materials (honeycomb, foam) — specification, approval and ongoing control.

- Own material preparation — cutting, kitting, ply-book adherence, prepreg freezer storage, out-time / out-life tracking and full material traceability from goods-in to lay-up.

- Operationally own and mould design, manufacture, maintenance and calibration, ensuring tools are fit for purpose and available to the production plan.

- Own mechanical and manual trimming and finishing of composite components.

Cross-plant collaboration and best practice transfer

- Build working relationships with your counterparts at our established production plants across Europe key learning of proven composite processes, tooling, lay-up and test methods.

- Lead knowledge-transfer exercises to capture, validate and adapt existing composite build processes, work instructions and lessons learned into your facility.

- Represent this facility's own innovations and lessons learned back into the network, so best practice flows in both directions.

Supply chain and outsourcing

- Work with Procurement/Supply Chain and Manufacturing Engineering to select material and outsourcing partners — resin, fibre, core and tooling — against cost, quality, lead time and supply security ensuring key component rate achievement is protected. Ensuring all outsourced materials and components meet quality standards.

Team build and leadership

- Recruit, build and lead the composites unit manufacturing team scaling in line with the production ramp.

- Define the team structure, role profiles, shift pattern and skills matrix; identify training needs and own the training plan.

- Onboard new team members set clear performance expectations and manage performance throughout.

- Build a culture of safety, ownership and continuous improvement within the team.

Quality and test

- Own documentation and quality assurance for the composites area — work instructions, ply-by-ply build records, cure records, batch and material traceability and non-conformance management.

- Own the inspection and test regimes — visual and dimensional inspection, NDT, witness and coupon testing — defining pass/fail criteria, test procedures and data capture ensuring every component that leaves the cell meets specification.

- Partner with the Quality function on root-cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, and non-conformance management and drive measurable improvement in first-pass yield, scrap and rework.

- Ensure the area operates within the relevant quality management system (e.g. AS9100 / ISO 9001) and any applicable safety or export-control requirements.

Production delivery

- Own the daily, weekly and monthly output of the composites area against the production plan delivering to schedule, to quality and to cost.

- Ensure production rate as volumes ramp is achieved, identifying and resolving constraints in real time.

- Run a structured day-start / shift routine with clear KPIs across safety, quality, delivery, cost and people.

- Plan and balance capacity across material preparation, lay-up, cure, trim, inspection and finishing.

Continuous improvement

- Own the lean operating system for the area: 5S, standard work, visual management and structured problem-solving and Kaizen.

- Lead improvement projects with measurable gains in safety, quality, throughput, lead time and cost.

- Use data to drive decisions, and champion a data-led approach across the team.

Health, safety and compliance

- Hold ultimate accountability for the safety of everyone working in the composites area, including resin, solvent and prepreg handling, cutting, trimming and cure operations.

- Ensure full compliance with UK health and safety legislation, COSHH for resins, hardeners and solvents, dust and fume extraction, fire safety around prepreg, ovens and autoclaves, and site procedures.

- Ensure correct PPE, handling and storage controls for composite materials, and safe operation of cutting, trimming and cure equipment.

What You'll Bring

Essential

- Experience in composites manufacture — aerospace, automotive, marine, motorsport, UAV/model aircraft or similar structural composite products.

- Practical, hands-on experience of both wet lay-up and pre-preg lay-up processes, including laminate, resin, fibre and core material selection and control.

- Experience in building a new manufacturing cell, line or facility including layout design, equipment selection, process definition and ramp to rate.

- Working knowledge of mechanical and manual trimming and finishing methods for composite components.

- A track record of recruiting, building and retaining a shop-floor or workshop team.

- Working knowledge of quality systems, documentation and material traceability in a regulated or precision-engineered environment.

- Practical continuous improvement experience: Lean, 5S, standard work, structured problem-solving.

- Confidence with ERP/MES systems and shop-floor data.

Desirable

- Experience working across a multi-site or multi-country manufacturing network, including transferring processes or best practice between plants.

- Comfortable with European travel and working with colleagues across languages and sites.

- Experience with additive manufacturing / 3D printing as a production support capability.

- Experience in aerospace, defence, motorsport or automotive composite structures manufacture.

- Experience commissioning a new factory, cell or line as part of a capacity expansion.

- Six Sigma Green Belt or above.

Customs & Transport Analyst

As our Customs & Transport Analyst, you will be the cornerstone of our international logistics and trade compliance operations. You will own end-to-end customs processes, ensure regulatory compliance across all import/export activities, and optimize our transport flows — with a high degree of independence and accountability for results.

This is a high-impact, hands-on role suited for a self-starter who thrives in a fast-paced, technically complex environment.

Location: Lisbon Office (on-site), with 2 weekly visits to our operational sites in Ponte de Sor, Leiria or Caldas da Rainha.

· Manage all import and export declarations, ensuring full compliance with national and international regulations (EU, US EAR/ITAR, dual-use goods, etc.)

· Classify products under the correct HS/HTS codes, with particular attention to UAV components and electronics

· Obtain and maintain necessary export licenses, permits, and authorizations

· Serve as the primary point of contact with customs authorities, freight forwarders, and brokers

· Collaborate with procurement, production, and sales teams to align logistics with business needs

Required Profile

· Tools: Proficiency with ERP systems, customs management software, and MS Office / Excel

We are establishing drone production in the United Kingdom and scaling it to full rate. Our new Swindon facility hosts the complete production lifecycle of our unmanned aircraft, alongside our other UK sites — and the logistics function that will feed, supply and ship this operation is yours to design and build. This is not a caretaker role: it is a rare opportunity for an industrial logistics leader to architect a multi-site network from near-blank paper — the strategy, the operating model, the systems, the partners and the team — and to scale it through an aggressive production ramp-up in a defence-critical environment.

The Role

The Country Head of Logistics is a senior leadership position with strategic accountability for the design, performance and growth of Tekever's UK logistics network, encompassing transport, customs and trade compliance, receiving, warehousing, line feeding, shipping and inventory. Across these areas, you will define the strategy, build the organisation, put in place the systems, partners and governance, and lead the managers who deliver operational excellence.

As a member of the UK operations leadership team, you will shape how logistics enables Tekever's industrial ramp-up: designing a multi-site network that can scale with production rates, representing logistics in S&OP and investment decisions, and positioning the function as a source of competitive advantage — in cost, speed, resilience and compliance.

- Logistics Strategy & Network Design — Define and own the UK logistics strategy and multi-year roadmap, aligned with Tekever's industrial strategy and production ramp-up plans; translate it into organisation, capability, infrastructure and investment plans.

- Operating Model — Design the target operating model across all sites: make-or-buy decisions (in-house vs 3PL), warehouse footprint and capacity planning, transport network architecture, and the service levels the function commits to internal and external customers.

- Organisation & Leadership — Build, lead and develop the logistics leadership team; define the organisational structure, roles and succession plans needed to scale from today's operation to full-rate production; instil a culture of safety, accountability and continuous improvement.

- Regulatory Compliance — Ensure that all logistics operations comply with applicable regulations and company policies, including UK customs rules, export controls for defence goods (UK Strategic Export Controls, ITAR), and dangerous goods requirements; embed compliant processes across transport, warehousing and shipping, and support audits and inspections in coordination with the company's trade compliance function.

- End-to-End Flow Ownership — Set the strategy, policies and performance framework for the end-to-end material flow — transport, customs, receiving, warehousing, line feeding, shipping and inventory — holding operational managers accountable for delivery against agreed KPIs.

- Executive Partnership — Represent logistics on the UK operations leadership team and in S&OP; partner with Procurement, Manufacturing, Quality, Programmes and Finance to ensure logistics is embedded in industrialisation decisions, new programme bids and customer commitments.

- Systems & Digitalisation — Define and drive the digital roadmap for logistics — ERP/WMS/TMS architecture, automation, data and analytics — to deliver visibility, scalability and decision-making capability across the network.

- A proven senior logistics or supply chain leader (typically 10+ years, with significant time in leadership roles) from manufacturing in aerospace, defence, automotive or another regulated, high-complexity industrial environment — ideally including production ramp-up, new-facility start-up or industrialisation programmes.

Mission

To own and drive risk and opportunity management across major Civil & Defence projects. The role is responsible for establishing and running the Risk and Opportunity Register, applying risk methodology and risk scoring and providing the Programme Director/SRO, Programme Manager and Chief Engineer with clear visibility, analysis and mitigation of programme, technical, regulatory, commercial and supply chain risk throughout delivery. The post holder will bring proven risk management experience from complex Defence, Aerospace and Engineering programmes, and the ability to work across programme, engineering, safety, commercial and supply chain disciplines to keep risk visible, owned and actively managed.

The Role:

Risk & Opportunity Management

1. Establish, own and maintain the Risk and Opportunity function.

2. Apply Risk methodology and risk scoring to classify, score and actively manage every risk, ensuring all has dedicated resource from across the organisation.

3. Facilitate risk identification workshops across programme, engineering, safety, commercial, supply chain and training functions, capturing new risks and opportunities as Projects progress.

4. Track mitigation actions to closure, escalating risks that exceed agreed tolerance thresholds to the Programme Manager and Programme Director/SRO.

Governance, Reporting & Assurance

1. Own risk and opportunity reporting into the Performance Review Meeting (PRM), Programme Board and Authority reporting cycle.

2. Maintain the Decision Log and supporting risk documentation, ensuring a clear audit trail of risk decisions and approvals.

3. Support programme controls (the PCMP and CWBS) by ensuring cost, schedule and quality risk are reflected in the integrated programme schedules and budgets.

4. Provide risk input into functional areas across the business.

Regulatory, Safety & Technical Risk Coordination

1. Coordinate with the Chief Engineer, Safety Manager and Airworthiness Lead to track engineering, safety and certification risk, including SAIL/OSO compliance, MRP adherence, and Design Organisation conformity across the UK/Portugal boundary.

2. Track integration and security risk associated with spiral development requirements, escalating critical-path issues to the Chief Engineer when required.

3. Track supply chain and production risk, including manufacturing readiness at WWA and Swindon, supplier lead times and single points of failure, working with the Supply Chain Lead and the Manufacturing, Assembly & Integration Lead.

4. Track commercial and IP risk, including contract change impact and Design Authority/IP transfer decisions, working with the Commercial Lead.

Internal Collaboration

1. Work closely with the Programme Manager and Programme Controls Manager to keep the Risk and Opportunity Register aligned with the wider programme schedule, budget and change control processes.

2. Support the Programme Director/SRO in preparing risk positions ahead of Authority engagement and negotiation.

3. Coach risk owners across the Delivery team in applying risk ensuring consistent approach across the business.

4. As is consistent with a scaling company, support work outside of core responsibilities where business priorities require. Tekever uses an Agile methodology that requires its workforce to adapt to changing work demands.

Competencies

Qualifications & Training

- Relevant professional experience in risk management, programme controls or project management within defence, aerospace or a comparable complex engineering sector.

- Formal risk management qualification (e.g. APM Risk, M_o_R, IRM) or equivalent.

- Undergraduate degree or equivalent professional experience in a relevant discipline.

Experience

- Proven experience establishing and running a risk on a complex programme, including risk identification, scoring, mitigation tracking and escalation.

- Experience reporting risk to senior governance boards and external customers/authorities.

- Experience with UK MOD or equivalent Defence procurement and governance.

- Experience on UAS, ISR or aerospace programmes involving multi-entity Design Authority arrangements.

Product / Domain Knowledge

- Understanding of risk management frameworks and tools (e.g. risk registers, probability/impact scoring, RAID logs) and the ability to apply them practically rather than passively.

- Familiarity with UAS/ISR systems, airworthiness and safety case concepts (MAA, SAIL/OSO, Def Stan 00-56).

- Familiarity with programme controls disciplines (CWBS, PCMP, earned value management).

· Solid experience with ROS2, including building nodes and wrappers to integrate sensors and other components.

We're looking for an experienced Technical Documentation Manager to join our growing Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) capability and lead the development, structure, and lifecycle management of technical publications for our Unmanned Air System (UAS) programmes. You'll take ownership of the technical documents, ensuring it is accurate, compliant, and delivered on schedule to support the airworthiness and in-service support of the platform.

Key Responsibilities

· Lead the planning, authoring, review, and approval of S1000D-compliant data modules across the publication lifecycle.

· Manage the Common Source Database (CSDB), associated data module code (DMC) structures and Data Module Requirements List (DMRL), ensuring correct classification, version control, and configuration management.

· Liaise with the customer and regulatory bodies to confirm documentation meets contractual and airworthiness requirements (e.g. MAA, Def Stan 00-600 series, or equivalent).

· Coordinate with engineering change processes to ensure documentation stays synchronised with design baselines.

· Defining and implementing a documentation strategy aligned with business objectives and standards.

· Support Interactive Electronic Technical Publication (IETP) delivery where applicable.

· Manage document reviews, sign-off cycles, and audit trails to support quality and configuration control.

· Report on documentation progress, risks, and milestones to programme leadership.

Qualifications, Experience & Commitments

· Familiarity with ASD S1000D Standards and experience managing S1000D-compliant technical documentation, ideally within defence or aerospace.

· Direct experience producing or managing an Air-System Document Set (ADS) or equivalent document set for a military or complex air platform.

· Experience working on a UAS/UAV/Defence programme, or a strong understanding of the unique documentation demands of unmanned/aerial platforms.

· Solid understanding of CSDB tools, data module structuring, and business rules implementation.

· Experience managing a technical authoring / publications team.

· Familiarity with configuration management and change control processes in a regulated environment.

· Strong knowledge of global documentation standards, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices inc. knowledge of Def Stan 00-600 series or equivalent NATO/MoD documentation standards.

· Experience with IETP authoring and viewer tools.

· Security Vetting: Due to the nature of our Defence contracts, all applicants must be eligible to hold and willing to undergo the vetting process for UK SC level Security Clearance.

· Travel: Willingness to undertake occasional national and international travel to TEKEVER sites (UK, Portugal, US, Europe) and potentially to deployed operations globally.

Skills & Attributes

· Solid technical expertise and attention to detail

· Strong stakeholder management skills, comfortable liaising with engineering, airworthiness, and customer representatives. Including balancing customer expectations against engineering realities and timescales

· Document planning and scheduling against programme milestones.

· Ability to manage external suppliers or subcontracted teams where required.

· Understanding of the wider engineering lifecycle — how design changes, safety cases, and support concepts feed into documentation

To support your wellbeing, we provide 25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays, Private Medical Insurance (with optional family cover), Private Dental care, and an Employee Assistance Programme. As a Remote Pilot you will play a critical role in the delivery of missions through monitoring flight operations, mitigating hazards performing real-time interventions and ensuring compliance with relevant regulations and standards.

You will be a team player, capable of operating within complex and challenging environments. You will drive improvement in TEKEVER products through continuous feedback on performance and limitations, and be passionate about solving problems to deliver excellence for our customers.

- Enforce adherence to company safety protocols and best practice

- A1 and A3 certificates (CAA/EASA)

- Engineering License

- Work authorisation in the UK is required.

- Language Requirements: Advanced proficiency in English, with proven fluency at the C2 level.

At TEKEVER, we offer a comprehensive package designed to reward, support, and develop our people. We are deeply committed to investing in future talent; our scale allows us to provide clear career development opportunities and dedicated initiatives to boost your skill sets, ensuring you remain future-ready for the evolving workplace.
